root_cause: The driver labels TIMEOUT_MS failures with the current stage but compares the deadline against _started_ms (process lifetime), not _stage_started_ms. B is the longest-lived client, so it can exhaust the global 150 s budget while legitimately reaching WAIT_CONVERGENCE_PEER late in the scenario. A2 starts much later and retains most of the same 150 s budget. This exactly matches repeated Windows failures at ~163-164 s total runtime and the historical WAIT_CONVERGENCE_PEER marker.
authorized_changes: Evaluate timeout against _stage_started_ms, which is already reset by _set_stage on every orchestration stage transition.
Include both stage_elapsed_ms and total_elapsed_ms in timeout evidence.
Add a contract assertion that the timeout clock is stage-scoped and not process-lifetime-scoped.
non_goals: Do not change runtime LEAVE or network protocol.
acceptance: Existing M5 contracts PASS including timeout-clock regression assertion.
Windows exact-Godot M5 stability 10/10 with no hidden reruns.
No M5_ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT occurs solely because total process lifetime exceeds 150 s while current stage is still within 150 s.
Only after Windows 10/10, run one canonical full world regression first attempt.
